# sophosfirewall_traffic_shaping_policy (Resource)

Manages a traffic shaping policy (*Configure > System services > Traffic shaping*). Policies are referenced by name, for example from `sophosfirewall_firewall_rule.qos.traffic_shaping_policy`. Only `description`, the rates of `bandwidth` and `scheduled_overrides` can be changed in place; changing anything else recreates the policy.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Cap each user at 10 Mbps, with a tighter limit during work hours.
resource "sophosfirewall_traffic_shaping_policy" "users" {
  name            = "Users-10M"
  description     = "Per-user cap"
  associates_with = "users"
  type            = "bestEffort"
  bandwidth = {
    limit = { aggregated_kbps = 10240 }
  }
  scheduled_overrides = [
    {
      schedule  = "Work hours (5 Day week)"
      bandwidth = { limit = { upload_kbps = 1024, download_kbps = 4096 } }
    },
  ]
}

# Guarantee 5 Mbps (burst to 20 Mbps) shared by all traffic of a rule.
resource "sophosfirewall_traffic_shaping_policy" "voip" {
  name            = "VoIP"
  associates_with = "rules"
  is_shared       = true
  type            = "guaranteed"
  bandwidth = {
    guaranteed = { aggregated_kbps = 5120 }
    limit      = { aggregated_kbps = 20480 }
  }
}

resource "sophosfirewall_firewall_rule" "voip" {
  name              = "voip"
  source_zones      = ["LAN"]
  destination_zones = ["WAN"]
  services          = ["SIP"]
  qos = {
    traffic_shaping_policy = sophosfirewall_traffic_shaping_policy.voip.name
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `associates_with` (String) What the policy is applied to. One of `users`, `rules`, `webCategories`, `applications`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `bandwidth` (Attributes) Bandwidth rates. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bandwidth))
- `name` (String) Unique name of the traffic shaping policy. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `type` (String) Policy type: `guaranteed` reserves a minimum bandwidth and can burst up to the limit, `bestEffort` only caps the bandwidth. One of `guaranteed`, `bestEffort`. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description.
- `is_shared` (Boolean) Bandwidth usage type: `true` shares one bandwidth pool among all matching users, rules, categories or applications, `false` gives each its own allocation (*Individual*). Defaults to `false`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `scheduled_overrides` (Attributes List) Bandwidth that applies instead of `bandwidth` while a schedule is active. Each override may use a different type and direction scope than the policy. Omit to leave the policy's overrides unmanaged. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scheduled_overrides))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID of the object assigned by the firewall.

<a id="nestedatt--bandwidth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bandwidth`

Required:

- `limit` (Attributes) Bandwidth limit: the cap of a best-effort policy or the burst ceiling of a guaranteed one (at least the guaranteed rate). Set either `aggregated_kbps`, or both `upload_kbps` and `download_kbps`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bandwidth--limit))

Optional:

- `guaranteed` (Attributes) Guaranteed minimum bandwidth. Required when `type` is `guaranteed`, not allowed for `bestEffort`. Set either `aggregated_kbps`, or both `upload_kbps` and `download_kbps`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bandwidth--guaranteed))

<a id="nestedatt--bandwidth--limit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bandwidth.limit`

Optional:

- `aggregated_kbps` (Number) Combined upload and download rate in kbps (16-20480000). Switching between `aggregated_kbps` and `upload_kbps`/`download_kbps` forces a new resource.
- `download_kbps` (Number) Download rate in kbps (16-20480000).
- `upload_kbps` (Number) Upload rate in kbps (16-20480000).


<a id="nestedatt--bandwidth--guaranteed"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bandwidth.guaranteed`

Optional:

- `aggregated_kbps` (Number) Combined upload and download rate in kbps (16-20480000). Switching between `aggregated_kbps` and `upload_kbps`/`download_kbps` forces a new resource.

- `upload_kbps` (Number) Upload rate in kbps (16-20480000).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by name or UUID.
terraform import sophosfirewall_traffic_shaping_policy.example <name-or-uuid>
```
